api/adapter.name: Adapter Over An External Service
api/adapter.usage: Use for the one file in a bounded context that leaves the process, whether that is a vendor SDK or a plain fetch.

api/adapter.name: External Service Adapter
api/adapter.usage: Use for the one file in a slice that talks to a third party SDK, so no other file imports the vendor package.

api/adapter.name: Adapter Over A Rate-Limited Web Service
api/adapter.usage: Use for the one file in a bounded context that calls a third-party HTTP service with a published rate limit.

api/controller.name: Controller Dispatch
api/controller.usage: Use for every Hono route. Validate input, call one service method, shape the response.

api/controller.name: Public Controller Router
api/controller.usage: Use for a router that is deliberately left ungated, so the reason is written where a reviewer looking for the missing guard will find it.

api/controller.name: Guarded Controller Router
api/controller.usage: Use for an administration router, so authentication is applied to every route of the chain before any handler can be reached.

api/controller.name: Controller File Response
api/controller.usage: Use for a route that answers with a downloadable file rather than json.

api/controller.name: Controller With Split Routers
api/controller.usage: Use for a slice whose routes do not all share one gate, so an ungated route cannot be mounted by mistake.

api/core.name: Core Projection
api/core.usage: Use for a read model that turns rows and `now` into the exact payload the caller sends.

api/core.name: Core Decision Function
api/core.usage: Use for every business rule. Take the data and `now` as arguments, return a decision, touch nothing else.

api/core.name: Core Lookup Table
api/core.usage: Use for a total mapping from a domain union onto values, so a new case is a type error rather than a missing branch.

api/core.name: Cross Cutting Helper Module
api/core.usage: Use for a rule no single slice owns. Put it under `helpers/<topic>/` and write down the envelope inside which its answers hold.

api/core.name: Core Parse Of Untrusted Input
api/core.usage: Use for the boundary where a third-party response becomes a typed domain value.

api/core.name: Core Serializer
api/core.usage: Use for rendering a text format. Take the data as arguments, return the whole string, read nothing else.

api/core.name: Core Parser With A Named Error
api/core.usage: Use for a hand written parser. Export its own error type and say in the header why no library does the job.

api/database.name: Database Schema Barrel
api/database.usage: Use for the one module the migration tool reads, so every table is named in a single place while each declaration stays inside the slice that owns it.

api/database.name: Database Client Singleton
api/database.usage: Use for the one module a repository imports to reach the database.

api/entrypoint.name: API Development Entrypoint
api/entrypoint.usage: Use for the local server of an API whose deployed form is a Lambda, so both start from the same composition root.

api/entrypoint.name: API Lambda Entrypoint
api/entrypoint.usage: Use for the Lambda handler of a Hono API. Build the app once, export the adapted handler, declare no route here.

api/entrypoint.name: Api Composition Root
api/entrypoint.usage: Use for the single module that mounts every slice router and whose inferred type is the front end's contract.

api/environment.name: Environment Reader
api/environment.usage: Use for collecting a slice's `process.env` reads into one module, so its pure files never reach for the environment themselves.

api/middleware.name: Middleware Session Gate
api/middleware.usage: Use for the gate a router applies to every route it carries.

api/repository.name: Repository Projection Constant
api/repository.usage: Use for a repository whose queries all return the same row shape.

api/repository.name: Repository Query
api/repository.usage: Use for data access. Drizzle queries and transactions only, and the single file allowed to import the database client for its slice.

api/repository.name: Repository Idempotent Upsert
api/repository.usage: Use for a write a caller may replay, so a fixture or a retry does not need a delete first.

api/repository.name: Repository Json Column Boundary
api/repository.usage: Use for a column holding json as text, which is what Aurora DSQL forces because it has no jsonb type.

api/repository.name: Repository Row Mapper
api/repository.usage: Use for a column wider than the domain type, so the narrowing happens once at the data boundary instead of at every read site.

api/schema.name: Schema With Table And Input
api/schema.usage: Use for a slice that owns a table, so its Drizzle definition and its Zod input schemas live in one file.

api/schema.name: Shared Slug Schema
api/schema.usage: Use for an identifier several slices validate, so the owning slice declares the rule once and the others import it.

api/schema.name: Schema With DSQL Constraints Written Down
api/schema.usage: Use for a table on Aurora DSQL, so every constraint the engine refuses is recorded beside the column with the guard that replaces it.

api/schema.name: Schema Without A Table
api/schema.usage: Use for a slice that persists nothing and still declares its input schema in the usual place.

api/service.name: Named Domain Error
api/service.usage: Use for a failure a caller has to tell apart, so the controller matches on the class rather than on the message text.

api/service.name: Service Orchestration
api/service.usage: Use for a workflow that reads, decides, then writes. The service is the only impure layer allowed to be interesting.

api/service.name: Service Patch Returning A Union
api/service.usage: Use for every partial update, so the controller maps arms to statuses instead of re-deriving why the write failed.

api/service.name: Service Facade Re-export
api/service.usage: Use for an error another module raises that the controller has to catch, so the controller still imports one module per slice.

api/service.name: Service Read Model
api/service.usage: Use for a query that assembles a view from several tables. Read everything, then let one pure function decide the shape.

api/service.name: Service DTO Mapping
api/service.usage: Use for turning a list of domain rows into DTOs when the mapper needs a value the environment holds.

api/service.name: Service Passthrough
api/service.usage: Use when a slice has no rule to apply yet and the controller still must not import the repository.

api/service.name: Service With Injected Clock
api/service.usage: Use for any service whose result carries a timestamp, so the value it returns is deterministic.

api/utils.name: DTO Mapper
api/utils.usage: Use for turning a domain object into the shape the front end receives, keeping the mapper pure so it carries the full coverage gate.

api/utils.name: Schema Refine Pure Helper
api/utils.usage: Use for the predicate behind a Zod `.refine`, so the rule sits in a covered sibling instead of an inline arrow function.

cdk/entrypoint.name: CDK Application Entry Point
cdk/entrypoint.usage: Use for the executable that turns the deploy environment into one CDK application tree.

cdk/entrypoint.name: Application CDK Stack
cdk/entrypoint.usage: Use for the module that composes the shared constructs into the infrastructure of one application.

infra/construct.name: Reusable CDK Construct
infra/construct.usage: Use for any piece of infrastructure more than one application stack composes.

infra/construct.name: CDK Custom Resource
infra/construct.usage: Use when a stack has to reach something CloudFormation has no resource type for, such as a database schema.

infra/stack.name: Shared Account Stack
infra/stack.usage: Use for a resource that exists once per AWS account and that other stacks need to find.

infra/unknown.name: CloudFront Function Source
infra/unknown.usage: Use for any code that runs on the CloudFront edge runtime rather than in Node.

infra/unknown.name: Custom Resource Handler
infra/unknown.usage: Use for the Lambda behind a CloudFormation custom resource.

infra/utils.name: Stage Wiring Selector
infra/utils.usage: Use whenever a construct would otherwise branch on the stage inline to decide what to wire.

infra/utils.name: Deploy Stage Guard
infra/utils.usage: Use for the first lines of any construct or naming helper that takes a stage.

site/adapter.name: Ref Callback Driving A Browser API
site/adapter.usage: Use for calling an imperative DOM method when React attaches a node, in place of a mount effect.

site/adapter.name: Adapter For A Direct Upload
site/adapter.usage: Use when the browser sends bytes to a storage service rather than to the application's own API.

site/atom.name: Plain Atom
site/atom.usage: Use for a user interface primitive that has one look and therefore needs no variant table.

site/atom.name: Atom With Lookup Variants
site/atom.usage: Use for a user interface primitive with several visual variants, composed without a variant library.

site/atom.name: Atom With Variant Table
site/atom.usage: Use for a user interface primitive with more than two visual variants.

site/atom.name: Null Rendering Atom
site/atom.usage: Use for the absent branch of a component lookup table, so the table has a component to name instead of a hole.

site/atom.name: Branchless Conditional Render
site/atom.usage: Use for showing or hiding a subtree without writing a ternary or a logical operator in the parent's markup.

site/atom.name: Atom Backed By An Icon Registry
site/atom.usage: Use for the single icon atom of an application, so every glyph the interface draws has one home.

site/client.name: Typed API Client
site/client.usage: Use for every call a front end makes to its own API. One client per application, built from the router type.

site/config.name: Workspace Test Configuration
site/config.usage: Use for the vitest configuration of a full stack workspace, where fast pure tests and serial database tests have to share one run.

site/core.name: Label Key Selector Core
site/core.usage: Use whenever a component needs the words for a domain value, so that the words themselves never reach the component.

site/core.name: Appearance Selector Core
site/core.usage: Use whenever a component would otherwise branch on a domain status to choose a colour, a class name, or a label key.

site/entrypoint.name: Site Entry Point
site/entrypoint.usage: Use for the module a browser loads first, which mounts React and nothing else.

site/hook.name: Effect Free Mount Hook
site/hook.usage: Use when work has to run exactly once per mount, in place of a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array.

site/i18n.name: Catalogue Parity Gate
site/i18n.usage: Use in every application shipping two catalogues, to fail the build on a key or a translation that was never written.

site/i18n.name: Translation Key Walk
site/i18n.usage: Use to turn a nested catalogue into the flat key list any catalogue check compares.

site/i18n.name: Typed Translation Keys Declaration
site/i18n.usage: Use once per application, so an unknown or renamed translation key fails the typecheck instead of rendering as itself.

site/i18n.name: i18n Runtime Setup
site/i18n.usage: Use for the module that builds the translation instance and keeps the document in step with the active language.

site/i18n.name: Injected Storage Slice
site/i18n.usage: Use when a module reads or writes a browser storage API and its logic still has to be testable without a browser.

site/molecule.name: Presentational Molecule
site/molecule.usage: Use for a molecule that renders what it is handed and decides nothing of its own.

site/molecule.name: Hook Over An External Store
site/molecule.usage: Use for reading a browser API into React, in place of an effect copying it into state.

site/molecule.name: Shared Props Shape Module
site/molecule.usage: Use when several interchangeable components must satisfy one props type that a lookup table can be typed against.

site/molecule.name: Molecule Reading The Shared Clock
site/molecule.usage: Use for a component whose display has to advance with wall clock time rather than with a data refetch.

site/molecule.name: Molecule Form Field
site/molecule.usage: Use for one labelled form control with its hint and its error message.

site/molecule.name: Molecule With A Selected View
site/molecule.usage: Use for a molecule that renders one of several shapes, where the choice depends on props plus one small piece of local state.

site/molecule.name: Molecule With Local State
site/molecule.usage: Use for a molecule that needs a small interface flag of its own, such as a drag highlight or an open toggle.

site/molecule.name: Molecule Dialog With A Form
site/molecule.usage: Use for a modal that edits a record and hands the result back to its parent.

site/organism.name: Presentational Organism
site/organism.usage: Use for a screen region that composes molecules and atoms but owns no state and fetches nothing.

site/organism.name: Core View Projection
site/organism.usage: Use for turning fetched data plus the current time into the exact list a component maps over.

site/organism.name: Organism That Owns A Query
site/organism.usage: Use for the lowest component allowed to call a query hook, where a screen region needs server data.

site/organism.name: Organism Dispatching Through A Table
site/organism.usage: Use for a screen region that owns state and has to choose which child renders the body.

site/organism.name: Organism Form
site/organism.usage: Use for a screen region that collects fields and writes them through a mutation.

site/organism.name: Core Form Schema And Payload
site/organism.usage: Use for the validation, the starting values and the request body of a form, kept out of the component that renders it.

site/organism.name: Route Form
site/organism.usage: Use for any form. One `useForm` call, fields as render props, and no field state in `useState`.

site/organism.name: Organism Mutation Panel
site/organism.usage: Use for a panel whose controls each fire a mutation and have to look applied before the server answers.

site/organism.name: Rule Exception With A Written Reason
site/organism.usage: Use whenever a rule has to be turned off for one line, after fixing the code and after scoping the rule in eslint.config.js have both been ruled out.

site/organism.name: Geometry Utilities Module
site/organism.usage: Use for the coordinate and distance maths behind a map, a chart, or any other drawn surface.

site/organism.name: Application Shell Organism
site/organism.usage: Use for the frame that wraps every routed page: the navigation, the global banners, and the outlet.

site/organism.name: Vendored Third Party Source
site/organism.usage: Use when source written elsewhere is copied into this repository rather than installed as a dependency.

site/organism.name: Organism Bound To A State Machine
site/organism.usage: Use for a screen region whose state lives in a hand written machine outside React.

site/organism.name: Hook Owning State And Returning Callbacks
site/organism.usage: Use for a piece of component state with its own small workflow, shared by more than one component.

site/organism.name: Organism With Headless Table
site/organism.usage: Use for a screen region showing tabular data with sorting or filtering.

site/organism.name: Organism Bridging An Imperative Library
site/organism.usage: Use for a third party library that owns a DOM node and needs to be created and torn down with it.

site/organism.name: Organism Driven By A State Machine
site/organism.usage: Use for a flow with several outcomes, where each step has to name why it happened rather than only whether it worked.

site/organism.name: Core Error To Translation Key
site/organism.usage: Use for turning a thrown value into the message a screen shows, without putting a status code in a component.

site/organism.name: Core Optimistic Overlay
site/organism.usage: Use for the local state that shows a write as applied before the server confirms it.

site/organism.name: Core Client State Machine
site/organism.usage: Use for a front end flow with several named outcomes, so the component stores one state instead of a set of flags.

site/query.name: Optimistic Mutation
site/query.usage: Use for a write whose new state the client can predict, so the change shows before the server answers.

site/query.name: Query Module
site/query.usage: Use for every call from a front end to its own API. One module per domain, holding the key factory and the hooks.

site/query.name: Uncached Mutation
site/query.usage: Use for a write whose result no cached query holds, so there is nothing to predict and nothing to invalidate.

site/query.name: Pessimistic Mutation
site/query.usage: Use for a write whose result the client cannot predict, such as an insert the caller reads an identifier back from.

site/query.name: Polling Query
site/query.usage: Use for data that several screens watch and that changes without this client writing it.

site/route.name: Core View Intent
site/route.usage: Use for a decision a route makes about what to do next, so the component holds no condition.

site/route.name: Route List Page
site/route.usage: Use for a route that reads a collection and renders it as a list or a grid.

site/route.name: Route Detail Page
site/route.usage: Use for a route that reads one record named by a route parameter.

site/route.name: Routing As A Table And A Parser
site/route.usage: Use for routing an application small enough not to want a router library.

site/types.name: Component Lookup Table
site/types.usage: Use for any render choice between two or more components, in place of a ternary or a `&&` in the markup.

site/types.name: Domain Types Module
site/types.usage: Use for the shapes a front end reads off its API, when those shapes are shared by several components.

site/unknown.name: Browser Edge Module
site/unknown.usage: Use for the one module that owns a browser system a React tree cannot hold, such as a timer, the history entry, or a canvas export.

site/unknown.name: Hand Edited Data Module
site/unknown.usage: Use for content a person edits and ships in a pull request, where there is no database and no content service behind the page.

site/unknown.name: External Store Module
site/unknown.usage: Use for state that lives outside React and that components read with `useSyncExternalStore`.

site/unknown.name: Observability Adapter
site/unknown.usage: Use for the one module a front end calls to report an event, so no component imports the vendor SDK.

site/unknown.name: Isolated Impure Edge Module
site/unknown.usage: Use for the randomness, timers or clock a mostly pure module needs, so the rest of it stays coverable.

site/unknown.name: Machine Singleton Module
site/unknown.usage: Use when one machine instance has to be reachable from components that share no common ancestor holding it.

site/unknown.name: Suspense Resource Module
site/unknown.usage: Use for data a route needs once per page load, where TanStack Query would be more machinery than the read is worth.

site/unknown.name: Persisted External Store Module
site/unknown.usage: Use for client state that several unrelated components read and that has to survive a reload.

site/utils.name: Pure Utility Module
site/utils.usage: Use for deterministic helpers with no side effect, which the coverage gate holds at one hundred percent per file.

site/utils.name: Formatter Utilities Module
site/utils.usage: Use for every number, date, and duration a screen shows, so no component formats a value inline.

site/utils.name: Seeded Generator Utility
site/utils.usage: Use for generative code, so that a module which draws random numbers still lives inside the purity gate.

site/utils.name: Unknown Payload Parser
site/utils.usage: Use for any boundary where a value arrives as `unknown`, such as storage, a fetch body, or a bundled JSON import.

site/utils.name: Hand Written State Machine Module
site/utils.usage: Use for session state that outlives a render, has timers of its own, and would otherwise be a tangle of `useState` and effects.

site/utils.name: Branchless Optional As A List
site/utils.usage: Use for a value that may be absent, or an action that only applies under a condition, so the caller iterates instead of branching.

site/utils.name: Injected Browser API Wrapper
site/utils.usage: Use for wrapping a browser capability that a test has to stand in for, such as geolocation, clipboard, or notifications.

site/utils.name: Satisfies Over Type Assertion
site/utils.usage: Use for a literal table that must match a declared type while keeping its own narrower inferred type.

test/api/adapter.name: Node Environment Adapter Test
test/api/adapter.usage: Use for a module that talks to a vendor SDK or reads `process.env`, so it runs under node rather than the default browser-like environment.

test/api/controller.name: Back End End To End Test
test/api/controller.usage: Use for a controller, exercising its routes through the real app against a live database.

test/api/database.name: Test Artifact Audit
test/api/database.usage: Use for a check on a generated file that ships, so the assertion is made about the file rather than about the objects that produced it.

test/api/middleware.name: Middleware Integration Test
test/api/middleware.usage: Use for a middleware, so it is exercised through a router of its own rather than through the routes of the real application.

test/api/repository.name: Repository Integration Test
test/api/repository.usage: Use for a repository or a service. Drive it against the real database with no HTTP transport in the way.

test/domain/core.name: Pure Unit Test
test/domain/core.usage: Use for every `*.core.ts` and `*.utils.ts` file, which the per-file coverage gate holds at 100 percent.

test/infra/unknown.name: Construct Synthesis Test
test/infra/unknown.usage: Use for every CDK construct. Synthesise once per stage, then assert on the CloudFormation template.

test/infra/unknown.name: Source Invariant Test
test/infra/unknown.usage: Use for a dantotsu eradication whose rule is a shape that must never reappear in a file, where no type or lint rule can express it.

test/infra/unknown.name: Handler Test Over A Mocked SDK
test/infra/unknown.usage: Use for a Lambda handler whose only collaborators are a third party SDK and a database driver.

test/site/atom.name: jsdom Gap Stub
test/site/atom.usage: Use when a component calls a browser API the test environment does not implement, and only then.

test/site/core.name: Exhaustive Domain Test
test/site/core.usage: Use for a function whose whole behaviour is a lookup keyed by a domain union, where every member has to be exercised.

test/site/i18n.name: Catalogue Parity Test
test/site/i18n.usage: Use as the sibling test of the parity gate, so an untranslated string cannot merge.

test/site/molecule.name: Component Render Test
test/site/molecule.usage: Use for asserting what a user sees and what their click does, rather than what the component called.

test/site/query.name: Query Hook Test
test/site/query.usage: Use for testing a query or mutation hook, including its optimistic write and its rollback.

test/site/unknown.name: Hook Probe Component
test/site/unknown.usage: Use to drive a custom hook from a test without pulling in a hook testing library.

test/site/unknown.name: Test Fixture Object Mother
test/site/unknown.usage: Use for building a complete valid domain object in one call, so a test states only the field its assertion is about.

test/site/unknown.name: Machine Test Driver
test/site/unknown.usage: Use to make a machine that owns timers and randomness fully deterministic, in a `.test-utils.ts` sibling the test glob does not pick up.

test/site/unknown.name: Test Database Isolation
test/site/unknown.usage: Use for giving every suite a clean database without rebuilding the schema, which is the expensive step.

test/site/unknown.name: Scenario End To End Test
test/site/unknown.usage: Use for a workflow whose meaning is the order events happen in, walked as one long case rather than split into independent ones.

test/site/unknown.name: Test Global Setup
test/site/unknown.usage: Use for the vitest `globalSetup` of a suite that needs a real database, with a paired teardown that releases whatever the setup started.

test/site/utils.name: State Machine Transition Test
test/site/utils.usage: Use for a hand written machine, to assert each command's effect on the snapshot rather than the calls it made.

test/tooling/lint-rule.name: Lint Rule Tester Suite
test/tooling/lint-rule.usage: Use for the suite that ships beside every custom lint rule.

tooling/lint-rule.name: Custom Lint Rule
tooling/lint-rule.usage: Use for a rule in the `borso` plugin that enforces one document in `docs/standards/`.

tooling/lint-rule.name: Shared Lint Rule Predicate
tooling/lint-rule.usage: Use for a question about a file or a node that more than one custom lint rule has to ask.
